title: Loss-aware typed group-1070 Binary DXF numeric output

authority.title: Autodesk About Extended Data
authority.finding: Describes 1070 as signed or unsigned 16-bit; these descriptions conflict on semantic domain.

differential.author: ezdxf 1.4.5 locally authored AC1024 LINE/XDATA inputs with XTEST APPID and following SENTINEL
differential.converter: ODA File Converter 27.1.0 verified native macOS executable, audit disabled
differential.observer: ezdxf 1.4.5 reads ODA Binary and subsequent ODA ASCII output; original sentinel follows each integer
differential.finding: ODA accepted all inputs and produced both outputs without .err. -32768 through 32767 kept their numeric values; positive 32768/40000/65535 became -32768/-25536/-1 in ODA Binary and ASCII readback while preserving the underlying 16-bit pattern. Do not claim ODA rejects unsigned values or that raw bits alone determine application interpretation.

implementation.policy: Typed XDATA and typed DWG-compatible XRECORD 1070 values above 32767 refuse Binary DXF before emission because the existing Binary reader exposes the value as signed int16, changing the typed numeric value. Signed-range Binary and ASCII output remain available. Existing low-level dxfWriterBinary and opaque/raw record paths still carry 16-bit patterns, including an explicitly requested 40000 pattern.
implementation.asciiBoundary: Existing dxfWriterAscii::writeInt16 and Binary counterpart already reject values outside [-32768,65535]. XDATA now checks that same range before writing the first group; ASCII accepted values are unchanged.
implementation.consumerCompatibility: No pure virtual, object layout, underlying Binary reader or low-level raw-bit behavior changed. The Binary typed API now fails rather than silently changing positive numeric values in 32768..65535; callers intending a raw bit pattern can use an opaque route or explicitly supply the equivalent signed value.

validation.result: PASS 1/1. Generated controls cover -32769, -32768, -1, 0, 32767, 32768, 40000, 65535 and 65536 in ASCII/Binary, no-prefix refusal, raw writer and opaque object bit transport, LINE XDATA and DWG-compatible XRECORD full-file destination rollback, caller-state preservation, same-codec corrected retry, and fresh typed readback.

limits: Bit-pattern equality does not establish application-level signedness; the policy is loss avoidance for the existing typed numeric API.
Opaque/raw replay intentionally retains bit transport and can expose signed-normalized typed values when read from Binary.
No source or generated DXF/DWG fixtures are committed.
